note: 50 plain-language physics facts for 'Did you know?' flyers (Studio.mountFact). Keep them checkable and jargon-free.
subject: physics
facts: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
Light travels about 300,000 kilometres every second. It could go around the Earth more than 7 times in one second.
A lightning bolt is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
You see lightning before you hear thunder because light is much faster than sound. Count the seconds and divide by 3 to find how many kilometres away the storm is.
Sound cannot travel through space. There is no air to carry it, so space is silent.
On the Moon you would weigh only about one sixth of what you weigh on Earth.
In 1971 astronaut David Scott dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon. With no air to slow them, they landed at the same time.
Water gets bigger when it freezes. That is why ice floats and why frozen bottles can crack.
Hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold water. It is called the Mpemba effect, after Erasto Mpemba, a schoolboy from Tanzania who noticed it.
At the equator, the Earth spins at about 1,670 kilometres per hour, yet we do not feel it.
The Earth races around the Sun at about 107,000 kilometres per hour.
A rainbow is sunlight split into colours by raindrops. You can only see one when the Sun is behind you.
The sky is blue because air scatters blue light much more than red light.
Sunsets look orange and red because the light passes through much more air, which scatters the blue away.
An atom is almost completely empty space.
If an atom were the size of a football stadium, its nucleus would be about the size of a pea in the centre.
Electrons in a wire move very slowly, often less than a millimetre per second, but the signal they carry moves almost as fast as light.
Messages in your nerves travel at up to about 120 metres per second. That is faster than a racing car.
Metal feels colder than wood in the same room because metal carries heat away from your hand much faster.
Cut a magnet in half and you get two magnets, each with its own north and south pole.
The Earth is a giant magnet. That is why a compass needle points north.
Victoria Falls drops about 108 metres. As the water falls, its stored energy turns into the energy of movement.
Kariba Dam on the Zambezi uses falling water to make electricity for Zimbabwe and Zambia.
Solar panels turn sunlight straight into electricity, with no moving parts.
Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize for showing that light comes in tiny packets, now called photons.
E = mc² means a tiny amount of mass holds a huge amount of energy.
Every second, the Sun turns about 4 million tonnes of its mass into light and heat.
When you look at a distant star, you may be seeing light that left it thousands of years ago.
A pendulum’s swing time depends on its length, not on how heavy it is.
An object keeps moving in a straight line unless a force stops it. This is Newton’s first law.
Seat belts save lives because your body keeps moving forward when a car stops suddenly.
Friction lets you walk. On perfectly smooth ice you could not push yourself forward at all.
A rocket moves forward by pushing hot gas backwards. Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
A boat floats because the water it pushes aside weighs as much as the boat. Archimedes worked this out over 2,000 years ago.
Diamonds sparkle because light bounces around many times inside them before it escapes.
The internet travels under the sea as flashes of light inside thin glass cables called optical fibres.
Your phone talks to the network with radio waves, a kind of light your eyes cannot see.
X-rays pass through skin and muscle but are stopped more by bone. That is why bones show up on an X-ray.
A microwave oven heats food by making the water in it jiggle faster.
Low gears on a bicycle make hills easier: you push with less force but turn the pedals more times.
With a long enough lever, you can lift something much heavier than yourself. Archimedes said: give me a place to stand and I will move the Earth.
The coldest possible temperature is minus 273.15 °C, called absolute zero. Nothing can get colder.
Water boils at a lower temperature on top of a mountain because the air pressure is lower there.
Black clothes get hotter in the sun because they soak up light. White clothes reflect most of it.
A flask keeps tea hot because a gap with no air in it stops heat escaping.
A spoon in a glass of water looks bent because light bends as it leaves the water.
Bats and dolphins find their food by listening to echoes of their own calls.
Ultrasound scans use sound too high for humans to hear to see a baby before it is born.
Young people can hear sounds from about 20 to 20,000 vibrations per second. Many animals hear much higher.
A jet that flies faster than sound, about 343 metres per second, makes a loud sonic boom.
